title: The Pilot
hook: Your group has seven days to make a TV show.

boss_suspicious.title: The boss thinks you're unhinged
boss_suspicious.description: Legal now attends rehearsals. Everything costs more when Legal is watching.

goose_grudge.title: The goose holds a grudge
goose_grudge.description: It believes it is the lead. It will not take notes.

haunted_laugh.title: The laugh track is haunted
haunted_laugh.description: It fires at every wrong moment. It has opinions.

s1.text: Day one of seven. The network has given you a studio, a budget and a deadline, in descending order of generosity. {spotlight} is holding the only pen that works.

choices.label: Pitch the talking dog show
choices.result: Everyone agrees it has been done. Everyone agrees to do it anyway.

choices.label: Pitch the gritty hospital drama
choices.result: Three people cry during the pitch. {spotlight} is fairly sure that is a good sign.

choices.label: Pitch whatever {randomPlayer} has been doodling
choices.result: It is a duck who solves crimes. {randomPlayer} has never looked so alive, and the room is suddenly on fire about it.

s2.text: Casting. There is one lead role and a room full of people who each privately believe they are the lead.

choices.label: {randomPlayer} carries the whole show
choices.result: {randomPlayer} accepts with a short speech nobody asked for.

choices.label: It's an ensemble, nobody is the lead
choices.result: Peace breaks out. Everyone quietly plans to steal every scene.

choices.label: The goose gets top billing
choices.result: There is no goose yet. The room decides this is a detail for later.

s3.text: The budget arrives in an envelope. Inside: four hundred euro and a voucher for a car wash. {spotlight} counts it twice.

choices.label: Spend it all on one extremely good chair
choices.result: The chair is magnificent. Nothing else in frame can look at it directly.

choices.label: Buy a smoke machine and hope
choices.result: The smoke machine has two settings: off, and weather event.

choices.label: Save it, somebody will need it later
choices.result: A dull decision that makes everyone feel obscurely safer.

s4.text: Props has delivered a goose. Nobody ordered a goose. The invoice says NO REFUNDS and, underneath, in different handwriting, GOOD LUCK.

choices.label: Write the goose into the script
choices.result: Act two is now substantially better and legally riskier.

choices.label: Let it roam and shoot around it
choices.result: The goose finds the one camera angle it likes and stays there.

choices.label: Put {randomPlayer} in charge of the goose
choices.result: {randomPlayer} and the goose reach an understanding that nobody else is allowed to know the terms of.

s5.text: Dress rehearsal. Act two collapses in a way that is, technically, new to television.

choices.label: Cut act two entirely
choices.result: The show is now nineteen minutes long. The network ordered twenty-two.

choices.label: Keep it and call it experimental
choices.result: You say the word "experimental" out loud and everyone relaxes immediately.

choices.label: Rewrite it overnight, together
choices.result: Nobody sleeps. The new act two is genuinely good, which feels unfair.

s6.text: The network boss walks in three days early. The set is on fire in a small, manageable, deeply illegal way, and the goose is loose.

choices.label: Pretend the fire is part of the show
choices.result: He watches the fire for a long moment. "Bold," he says, in the voice of a man updating a spreadsheet.

choices.label: Distract him with the catchphrase
choices.result: {spotlight} lands it perfectly. He laughs. The fire is dealt with off-camera by somebody braver.

choices.label: Get the entire cast to perform a musical number
choices.result: Nobody rehearsed this. Somehow that helps. He applauds through the whole thing, and props put the fire out during the key change.

s7.text: The boss leaves in a good mood. You have four days, one goose, and a set that smells faintly of victory and smoke.

choices.label: Push for a bigger finale
choices.result: The finale now requires a crane you do not have.

choices.label: Lock the script and protect what works
choices.result: A calm, professional decision. It will be the only one.

s7b.text: The boss left without saying goodbye. Someone from Legal has started attending rehearsals with a clipboard and no expression.

choices.label: Charm Legal
choices.result: Legal laughs once, writes it down, and underlines it.

choices.label: Ignore Legal and work faster
choices.result: Legal turns a page. Nobody has seen the first page.

s8.text: The show needs a title. The network wants it by five o'clock. It is four o'clock.

choices.label: Duck, Duck, Hospital
choices.result: It tests badly with everyone except one focus group who will not stop talking about it.

choices.label: The Goose Is Out
choices.result: Legally this implies the goose was ever contained.

choices.label: Just call it Untitled
choices.result: Marketing loves it. Marketing is the only one.

s9.text: Shooting day. {spotlight} is calling the shots and {randomPlayer} has already lost a shoe somewhere in the rig.

choices.label: Shoot the whole thing in one long take
choices.result: Take one is a disaster. Take nine is a miracle. There is no take ten.

choices.label: Cover everything, fix it in the edit
choices.result: Four hours of footage, all of it usable, none of it exciting.

choices.label: Let the goose improvise
choices.result: The goose improvises. It is the best footage you have. The goose now knows it is the best footage you have.

s10.text: Broadcast night. Ninety seconds to air. The lead has lost their voice, the goose is in the lighting rig, and the network boss is sitting in the front row.

choices.label: Go live and pray
choices.result: You go live. The laugh track fires at every wrong moment and will not stop. It is still going quietly under the credits.

choices.label: Send {randomPlayer} out to stall
choices.result: {randomPlayer} stalls for four minutes with a story about a dog. It is, unexpectedly, the best-reviewed part of the night.

choices.label: Rewrite the cold open live, on air
choices.result: {spotlight} rewrites it out loud while the camera is running and everyone follows. The goose stays in the rig, watching, like a producer.

s11.text: The morning after. The overnight numbers arrive in an envelope thinner than anyone wanted. {spotlight} opens it.

choices.label: Read them out loud
choices.result: {spotlight} reads. The room goes very quiet, and then does not.

choices.label: Hand them to {randomPlayer} without looking
choices.result: {randomPlayer} reads, makes a face nobody can interpret, and turns the page around.

endings.title: Renewed for nine seasons
endings.text: Not one disaster made it to air. The network orders nine seasons and a holiday special that nobody will enjoy making.

endings.title: Midseason replacement
endings.text: One thing went visibly wrong and the show survived it. It airs in February against something enormous and does better than anyone expected. The goose is invited back.

endings.title: Burned off over two nights in August
endings.text: Two disasters, both on camera. The network airs it quietly, out of order, opposite the tennis. Somebody, somewhere, tapes it.

endings.title: Cancelled, now a cult classic
endings.text: Everything that could go wrong went wrong on camera. Eleven years later a bootleg is passed around and the phrase “the goose episode” enters the language.
